mechanism_name: SOL US-session attention-phase continuation (diurnal participation-composition double difference)
mechanism_story: Who is slow to react: the US-retail long tail that dominates SOLUSDT's participant mix. SOL is the attention alt: its perp audience skews to leveraged retail and notification-driven traders, whereas BTC/ETH flow is institution-weighted and distributed across the whole UTC day. Why the effect exists: retail attention is diurnal — it concentrates inside the US afternoon/evening window (14:00-21:00 UTC) when that cohort is active and social feeds amplify whatever SOL did that day. Each retail participant discovers a SOL move only after it is already visible and decides on their own clock, so their inbound orders arrive STAGGERED over the following UTC day(s); the day's attention mark therefore propagates into next-day buying rather than being fully priced at the US close. The observable that measures it is a pure participation-COMPOSITION double difference: SOL's share of its own daily trade COUNT falling inside the US window, minus the majors' (BTC+ETH pooled) share of theirs over the same window, from completed day t-1. Count share (not aggressor split, not volume level, not price) isolates WHERE participation landed from HOW MUCH traded and WHO initiated. When the anchor trades, it is because SOL's activity is disproportionately US-timed relative to the majors' own diurnal profile — retail-attention-led, not institution-led. When it must fail: (i) when US-concentrated activity is a market-wide event, majors' profiles co-move with SOL's, the double difference collapses toward 0 and the book stands aside (self-protecting); the residual fatal condition is a regime where next-day SOL flow is dominated by non-US institutional desks that fade an exhausted retail mark (late-cycle crowding after extended SOL runs), inverting the continuation; (ii) cost domination: if staggered next-day continuation per completed hold is smaller than the tier-2.0 round trip, the book dies even though the drift exists. Novelty posture (measured, not argued, at D2): the conditioning series is a within-day count-share composition, orthogonalized against the majors' profile; it contains no return, aggressor, large-trade, run, displacement, or raw-volume-level term, so it is not a re-label of any packet section 4 family at any clock.
universe: BTCUSDT, ETHUSDT, SOLUSDT (the 3-symbol panel; SOLUSDT is the only traded symbol, BTCUSDT+ETHUSDT enter solely as the majors' diurnal-normalisation reference)
clock: daily (decision at the UTC 00:00 day boundary; daily-or-slower per axis-2 grant)
warmup: 61 daily decisions for the anchor (60-completed-day rolling median burn-in for the threshold + 1 completed day of composition input); 91 for the neighbour (90-day median). No decision is emitted, and no position held, before the warmup completes inside each fold.
features_and_lags: Inputs (section 2 columns only): n_trades for BTCUSDT, ETHUSDT, SOLUSDT at H1 grain. Derived per completed UTC day d and hour h: n_SYM(d,h) = SUM(n_trades) over rows with symbol=SYM, day_utc=d, hour_utc=h. Availability law: the decision at 00:00 UTC of day t uses ONLY rows with close_ts <= t, i.e. the 24 completed H1 buckets of day t-1 (lag 1..24 hours) plus the trailing 60 completed days t-60..t-1 for the rolling median; no same-bucket or same-day rows enter the decision. All fills are explicitly next-bucket-open (day t bucket-0 VWAP, close_ts 01:00 UTC), so no same-bucket close is ever consumed by a fill decision.
entry_exit_fills: Entry: at decision t, if the anchor state is ON (e_{t-1} > trailing 60-day median of e), buy 1.0x notional SOLUSDT perp at day t bucket-0 VWAP (close_ts 01:00 UTC); else hold flat. Exit/holding: position held until the state turns OFF; with H=1 every day re-decides at 00:00, and an OFF decision closes the position at that day's bucket-0 VWAP; an unchanged state triggers NO fill (hold-through). Force-flat: any position still open at the final decision of a fold is closed at that fold's last tradable H1 bucket VWAP (the bucket whose close_ts equals the fold's last day boundary); no position ever crosses a fold boundary or the +/-1-day purge gap. Fill timing: every fill (entry and exit) is a taker fill at the H1 bucket-0 VWAP following the decision instant — the explicitly next-bucket-open default; no same-bucket close peeking.
costs: Acknowledged: taker fee is charged EXACTLY ONCE PER FILL (L-V14-0) — each entry and each exit is one fill, one fee; no maker assumptions, no fee netting, no intra-bucket averaging of fees. Cost book: TIER 2.0 IS THE PRIMARY BOOK (fee 5.0 bps x 2.0 = 10.0 bps per fill, slip floor 2 ticks); tiers x1.0 and x1.5 are reported as sensitivity only. Stress multipliers apply to BOOKED PnL.
anchor: Daily long/flat book on SOLUSDT. At each UTC 00:00 decision t in S0 (after warmup): (1) from the completed day t-1 H1 rows compute s_h = n_SOL(t-1,h)/SUM_k n_SOL(t-1,k) and m_h = (n_BTC(t-1,h)+n_ETH(t-1,h))/SUM_k (n_BTC(t-1,k)+n_ETH(t-1,k)) for k=0..23; (2) e_{t-1} = SUM_{h=14}^{21} (s_h - m_h); (3) theta_{t-1} = median of e over the trailing 60 completed days (t-60..t-1); (4) if e_{t-1} > theta_{t-1}, long 1.0x notional SOLUSDT perp, else flat. State changes execute as taker fills at day t bucket-0 VWAP per entry_exit_fills. Frozen parameters: US window W = hours 14..21 UTC (8 hours), median window 60 days, hold H=1 day, long-only, no leverage scaling.
neighbour: Same mechanism, different frozen parameters: US window W' = hours 13..22 UTC (10-hour), threshold = trailing 90-day median of e (same formula), minimum hold 2 days — a position exits only at a decision where the state is OFF AND the position has been held for >= 2 complete UTC days; all else identical (same columns, same lag law, same fills, same force-flat). Tests robustness of the attention-phase effect to window width, threshold horizon, and holding period without re-tuning anything else.
control: Randomized session-boundary sham (the packet's named control class for session-conditioned books). Identical book in every respect, except the diurnal alignment of the window is destroyed: on each day t the window offset k_t = (day_index of t from 2025-08-22) mod 24 is applied, i.e. the sham computes SUM_{h in (W + k_t) mod 24} (s_h - m_h) — the SAME double-difference profile evaluated over a rotated 8-hour block, with every hourly activity level and the day's cross-sectional structure preserved. Across 365 days the frozen rotation cycles through all 24 offsets, so the sham asks 'does ANY 8-hour block work, or specifically the real US block?'. This is the convenient explanation that must NOT reproduce the anchor: if the edge were generic block-composition noise rather than US-session retail attention, the sham book earns the same expectancy. Sham decision/fill/cost machinery is byte-identical to the anchor's.
exposure_series_spec: Daily conditioning exposure series for D2 (exact formula over panel columns): e_t = SUM_{h=14}^{21} [ n_SOL(t-1,h)/SUM_{k=0}^{23} n_SOL(t-1,k) - (n_BTC(t-1,h)+n_ETH(t-1,h))/SUM_{k=0}^{23} (n_BTC(t-1,k)+n_ETH(t-1,k)) ], where n_SYM(d,h) = SUM(n_trades) over H1 rows with symbol=SYM, day_utc=d, hour_utc=h; series defined for every decision day t in S0 with t-1 >= 2025-08-22 (one value per UTC day; the value dated t reflects day t-1 information). D2 pools e_t (and the neighbour variant with window {13..22}) against the full forbidden-inventory exposure set; pooled |rho| <= 0.20 required.
falsification_rule: Pre-registered and mechanical; the family DIES if ANY of: (F1) G11 — the randomized session-boundary sham reproduces the anchor on pooled S0 after tier-2.0 costs: same expectancy sign AND |sham expectancy| >= 0.5 x |anchor expectancy|; (F2) anchor G1: pooled after-cost expectancy <= 0 at tier 2.0; (F3) D2 novelty veto: pooled |rho| > 0.20 between the exposure series e_t (anchor and neighbour variants as specified) and ANY forbidden-inventory conditioning exposure; (F4) anchor G2: pooled PF < 1.10. No re-windowing, re-clocking, hour-shift, sign-flip, symbol-subset or threshold-weakening rescue is permitted after any F fires; a dead family is dead at every parameterisation of this mechanism.
expected_failure_interpretation: A REJECT means SOL's diurnal attention composition carries no after-cost next-day continuation. Specifically: F1 implies the edge is generic block-composition noise, not US-session retail attention; F2/F4 imply staggered retail arrival is too weak to clear taker costs at tier 2.0 even if present; F3 implies the count-share composition is statistically a repackaging of a dead exposure (most plausibly the dollar-volume/activity-level family, since both are built from activity aggregates — this is the most likely kill mode and is accepted in advance). In every case the conclusion is that WHERE SOL participation lands in the UTC day has no incremental after-cost information; the family is closed at all clocks, windows and symbol subsets.
expected_failure_mode: Cost domination (the named risk of this frontier). Turnover estimate per decision: the long/flat state is persistent (crossings of a slow 60-day median of a composition series), est. 30-45 state changes per 365 decisions = 0.08-0.12 changes per decision-day, each change = 1 exit + 1 entry taker fill, i.e. ~0.16-0.25 taker fills per decision-day (~60-90 fills per S0 year, average hold ~4-6 days). At tier 2.0 (10.0 bps per fill + 2-tick slip floor) that is ~6.0-9.0% annual cost drag at full notional, so each completed hold must gross >= ~30 bps (>= ~5-6 bps per held day on SOL's ~4-5% daily vol) to survive; if the staggered-arrival drift is thinner than that, the book dies by cost domination before any statistical verdict is reachable. This is the primary expected failure mode.
